protocols.name: Construct steering vectors from paired-activation differences
protocols.detail: Collect residual activations on identical prompts from two conditions (e.g., base vs finetuned), compute per-prompt Δ=h_f−h_0 at selected tokens, and average per layer to form steering vectors; exclude generated-answer tokens if relevant.

protocols.name: Low-rank PCA with energy calibration
protocols.detail: PCA the centered per-sample differences per layer, keep top-k components, align signs, and rescale to preserve intervention energy after truncation; sweep k.

controls.name: Parameter-updated baseline on same data (full/LoRA/LoRRA finetuning)
controls.detail: Train a parameter-updated model on the same targets/data used to derive the steering vectors and evaluate under the same setup.
controls.rules_out: That the effect is simply what fine-tuning would produce rather than an activation-steering-specific phenomenon.

controls.name: Prompt-only/system-prompt control
controls.detail: Apply only the system/prompt intervention (no activation edit) under the same multi-turn protocol.
controls.rules_out: That long-context/KV-cache persistence or prompting alone explains drift or coherence changes attributed to steering.
evidence: Prompt-Activation Duality: Improving Activation Steering via Attention-Level Interventions

controls.name: Directionality control with size-matched randomized/permuted vectors
controls.detail: Construct a control vector by permuting or randomizing the components per layer while preserving mean/std or total norm.
controls.rules_out: That equal-magnitude activation perturbations (rather than the learned direction) account for the effect.
evidence: Extending Activation Steering to Broad Skills and Multiple Behaviours

controls.name: Injection-depth ablations and equal-budget schedules
controls.detail: Apply the same steering budget at different layers/windows or distribute it across depth using alternative schedules (random, uniform, box) under equal total norm.
controls.rules_out: That any perturbation location or total energy alone explains results; isolates sensitivity to where and how strength is allocated.
evidence: Activation Steering Induces Emergent Misalignment: A More Comprehensive Evaluation
Depth-Wise Activation Steering for Honest Language Models

controls.name: Single-layer vs depth-wise scheduled steering
controls.detail: Compare a point-mass single-layer edit to a depth-wise schedule matched for total norm.
controls.rules_out: That improvements are explained by simply injecting a vector (single layer) rather than by the depth-wise allocation.
evidence: Depth-Wise Activation Steering for Honest Language Models

controls.name: Equal-energy low-rank vs full-dimensional vector
controls.detail: Project the steering vector onto top-k PCA components with energy calibration and compare to the full vector at matched energy.
controls.rules_out: That apparent gains or losses are due to reduced vector energy rather than concentrating on informative low-rank directions.
evidence: Activation Steering Induces Emergent Misalignment: A More Comprehensive Evaluation

controls.name: Established steering-method baselines
controls.detail: Evaluate ActAdd (activation addition), Mean/Linear-AcT, DIM, ITI/ITI-C, RePE, CAA, AURA under the same data and metrics.
controls.rules_out: That gains are due to dataset/setup idiosyncrasies rather than the proposed steering mechanism outperforming prior methods.
evidence: Activation Steering with a Feedback Controller

controls.name: Uniform full-layer steering vs segmented layer-group tuning
controls.detail: Apply a single fusion/strength parameter across all layers versus separately tuned parameters for early/mid/late layer groups.
controls.rules_out: That improvements are due merely to any across-the-board activation injection rather than layer-group-specific control.
evidence: Fusion Steering: Prompt-Specific Activation Control

controls.name: Residual-stream activation-add baseline
controls.detail: Add a fixed persona/behavior vector to the residual stream at a single site with tuned α and compare to attention-level steering.
controls.rules_out: That any activation-add steering suffices, isolating the contribution of the alternative pathway (e.g., attention-delta with gating/cropping).
evidence: Prompt-Activation Duality: Improving Activation Steering via Attention-Level Interventions

confounds.name: Fluency/overlap improvements mistaken for target-behavior change
confounds.detail: Higher fluency or lexical overlap can inflate harmfulness/accuracy proxies without genuinely changing the targeted behavior.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Measure harmfulness independently from coherence (require both for 'coherent-harmful'), report human MOS/SpkSIM, and use composite metrics combining token overlap with LLM-graded quality.
evidence: Activation Steering Induces Emergent Misalignment: A More Comprehensive Evaluation
EmoShift: Lightweight Activation Steering for Enhanced Emotion-Aware Speech Synthesis
Fusion Steering: Prompt-Specific Activation Control

confounds.name: General capability degradation (alignment tax) explains effects
confounds.detail: Global degradation (e.g., higher PPL, lower task accuracy) could reduce targeted outputs and mimic successful steering.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report PPL on fixed text, MMLU, and Pile top-1 while steered; show targeted changes with minimal utility loss.
evidence: Activation Steering with a Feedback Controller
Extending Activation Steering to Broad Skills and Multiple Behaviours

confounds.name: Evaluator dependence (classifier vs LLM judge)
confounds.detail: Observed toxicity or safety changes might depend on the chosen evaluator rather than reflect real behavior changes.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Evaluate with both a classifier and multiple LLM judges and report both.
evidence: Activation Steering with a Feedback Controller

confounds.name: Overfitting to prompts used to compute steering directions
confounds.detail: Directions may overfit training prompts, inflating evaluation on similar items.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use disjoint train/validation/test splits (e.g., 80/20 for ADVBENCH, separate splits for behavior datasets) and report held-out performance.
evidence: Activation Steering with a Feedback Controller

confounds.name: Steering effects are identical to fine-tuning
confounds.detail: If steering merely reproduces fine-tuned behavior, it offers no distinct mechanism/benefit.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Directly compare steered vs fine-tuned models on the same metrics; include LoRA/LoRRA/full fine-tune baselines.
evidence: Activation Steering Induces Emergent Misalignment: A More Comprehensive Evaluation
Depth-Wise Activation Steering for Honest Language Models

confounds.name: Magnitude-only perturbation (not direction) drives results
confounds.detail: Equal-norm or equal-statistic activation changes might produce similar outcomes without relying on learned directionality.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use per-layer permuted vectors preserving mean/std or randomized equal-norm controls; compare against true direction.
evidence: Extending Activation Steering to Broad Skills and Multiple Behaviours

confounds.name: Mode collapse or invalid outputs misread as success
confounds.detail: Strong steering can induce invalid or collapsed outputs that confound behavior scores.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Filter/penalize settings with >5% faulty outputs or >95% single-token frequency and report penalties.
evidence: Extending Activation Steering to Broad Skills and Multiple Behaviours

confounds.name: Coherence drift caused by long context/KV persistence, not steering
confounds.detail: Accumulated context alone could degrade coherence over turns.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Run prompt-only and no-steering baselines under identical multi-turn protocols; show stability relative to steered runs.
evidence: Prompt-Activation Duality: Improving Activation Steering via Attention-Level Interventions

confounds.name: Improved coherence due to weaker steering signal
confounds.detail: A method might avoid drift just by reducing effective steering strength, sacrificing trait expression.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report trait-expression alongside coherence across turns; show maintained or improved trait strength.
evidence: Prompt-Activation Duality: Improving Activation Steering via Attention-Level Interventions

confounds.name: Response-token contamination in extracted vectors causes drift
confounds.detail: Response-dependent components in vectors may drive KV cache accumulation unrelated to intended prompt signal.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Ablate cropping (remove response-token contributions) and gating to show their effect on drift; restoring response tokens increases drift.
evidence: Prompt-Activation Duality: Improving Activation Steering via Attention-Level Interventions

confounds.name: Low-rank effects due to reduced intervention energy
confounds.detail: Performance changes after low-rank projection may stem from lower vector energy, not informative subspace selection.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Energy-calibrate the low-rank projection to match full-vector energy and then compare.
evidence: Activation Steering Induces Emergent Misalignment: A More Comprehensive Evaluation

confounds.name: Controller overshoot/instability masks practical failures
confounds.detail: Integral action may remove bias but create large overshoot oscillations that hide instability.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Measure error alignment across layers and compare P, PI, and PID to show reduced overshoot with PID.
evidence: Activation Steering with a Feedback Controller

confounds.name: Classifier-driven artifacts in emotion metrics
confounds.detail: SER gains may reflect optimization toward the classifier rather than perceptible emotion.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Human AB intensity tests and MOS/Emo-MOS alongside SER.
evidence: EmoShift: Lightweight Activation Steering for Enhanced Emotion-Aware Speech Synthesis

confounds.name: Selection bias from focusing only on incorrect cases
confounds.detail: Restricting to initially incorrect prompts may skew topic distribution and inflate gains.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare topic distributions of the full and selected subsets and show alignment.
evidence: Fusion Steering: Prompt-Specific Activation Control

controls.name: Residual-stream activation-add baseline
evidence: Prompt-Activation Duality: Improving Activation Steering via Attention-Level Interventions
controls.detail: Add a fixed persona/behavior vector to the residual stream at a single site with tuned α and compare to attention-level steering.
controls.rules_out: That any activation-add steering suffices, isolating the contribution of the alternative pathway (e.g., attention-delta with gating/cropping).

controls.name: Single-layer vs depth-wise scheduled steering
evidence: Depth-Wise Activation Steering for Honest Language Models
controls.detail: Compare a point-mass single-layer edit to a depth-wise schedule matched for total norm.
controls.rules_out: That improvements are explained by simply injecting a vector (single layer) rather than by the depth-wise allocation.

controls.name: Uniform full-layer steering vs segmented layer-group tuning
evidence: Fusion Steering: Prompt-Specific Activation Control
controls.detail: Apply a single fusion/strength parameter across all layers versus separately tuned parameters for early/mid/late layer groups.
controls.rules_out: That improvements are due merely to any across-the-board activation injection rather than layer-group-specific control.

confounds.name: Fluency/overlap improvements mistaken for target-behavior change
evidence: Activation Steering Induces Emergent Misalignment: A More Comprehensive Evaluation
EmoShift: Lightweight Activation Steering for Enhanced Emotion-Aware Speech Synthesis
Fusion Steering: Prompt-Specific Activation Control
confounds.detail: Higher fluency or lexical overlap can inflate harmfulness/accuracy proxies without genuinely changing the targeted behavior.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Measure harmfulness independently from coherence (require both for 'coherent-harmful'), report human MOS/SpkSIM, and use composite metrics combining token overlap with LLM-graded quality.

confounds.name: General capability degradation (alignment tax) explains effects
evidence: Activation Steering with a Feedback Controller
Extending Activation Steering to Broad Skills and Multiple Behaviours
confounds.detail: Global degradation (e.g., higher PPL, lower task accuracy) could reduce targeted outputs and mimic successful steering.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report PPL on fixed text, MMLU, and Pile top-1 while steered; show targeted changes with minimal utility loss.

confounds.name: Steering effects are identical to fine-tuning
evidence: Activation Steering Induces Emergent Misalignment: A More Comprehensive Evaluation
Depth-Wise Activation Steering for Honest Language Models
confounds.detail: If steering merely reproduces fine-tuned behavior, it offers no distinct mechanism/benefit.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Directly compare steered vs fine-tuned models on the same metrics; include LoRA/LoRRA/full fine-tune baselines.

confounds.name: Classifier-driven artifacts in emotion metrics
evidence: EmoShift: Lightweight Activation Steering for Enhanced Emotion-Aware Speech Synthesis
confounds.detail: SER gains may reflect optimization toward the classifier rather than perceptible emotion.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Human AB intensity tests and MOS/Emo-MOS alongside SER.

confounds.name: Coherence drift caused by long context/KV persistence, not steering
evidence: Prompt-Activation Duality: Improving Activation Steering via Attention-Level Interventions
confounds.detail: Accumulated context alone could degrade coherence over turns.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Run prompt-only and no-steering baselines under identical multi-turn protocols; show stability relative to steered runs.

confounds.name: Controller overshoot/instability masks practical failures
evidence: Activation Steering with a Feedback Controller
confounds.detail: Integral action may remove bias but create large overshoot oscillations that hide instability.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Measure error alignment across layers and compare P, PI, and PID to show reduced overshoot with PID.

confounds.name: Evaluator dependence
evidence: Activation Steering with a Feedback Controller
confounds.detail: Observed toxicity or safety changes might depend on the chosen evaluator rather than reflect real behavior changes.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Evaluate with both a classifier and multiple LLM judges and report both.

confounds.name: Improved coherence due to weaker steering signal
evidence: Prompt-Activation Duality: Improving Activation Steering via Attention-Level Interventions
confounds.detail: A method might avoid drift just by reducing effective steering strength, sacrificing trait expression.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report trait-expression alongside coherence across turns; show maintained or improved trait strength.

confounds.name: Low-rank effects due to reduced intervention energy
evidence: Activation Steering Induces Emergent Misalignment: A More Comprehensive Evaluation
confounds.detail: Performance changes after low-rank projection may stem from lower vector energy, not informative subspace selection.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Energy-calibrate the low-rank projection to match full-vector energy and then compare.

confounds.name: Magnitude-only perturbation (not direction) drives results
evidence: Extending Activation Steering to Broad Skills and Multiple Behaviours
confounds.detail: Equal-norm or equal-statistic activation changes might produce similar outcomes without relying on learned directionality.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use per-layer permuted vectors preserving mean/std or randomized equal-norm controls; compare against true direction.

confounds.name: Mode collapse or invalid outputs misread as success
evidence: Extending Activation Steering to Broad Skills and Multiple Behaviours
confounds.detail: Strong steering can induce invalid or collapsed outputs that confound behavior scores.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Filter/penalize settings with >5% faulty outputs or >95% single-token frequency and report penalties.

confounds.name: Overfitting to prompts used to compute steering directions
evidence: Activation Steering with a Feedback Controller
confounds.detail: Directions may overfit training prompts, inflating evaluation on similar items.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use disjoint train/validation/test splits (e.g., 80/20 for ADVBENCH, separate splits for behavior datasets) and report held-out performance.

confounds.name: Response-token contamination in extracted vectors causes drift
evidence: Prompt-Activation Duality: Improving Activation Steering via Attention-Level Interventions
confounds.detail: Response-dependent components in vectors may drive KV cache accumulation unrelated to intended prompt signal.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Ablate cropping (remove response-token contributions) and gating to show their effect on drift; restoring response tokens increases drift.

confounds.name: Selection bias from focusing only on incorrect cases
evidence: Fusion Steering: Prompt-Specific Activation Control
confounds.detail: Restricting to initially incorrect prompts may skew topic distribution and inflate gains.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare topic distributions of the full and selected subsets and show alignment.

experiment_recipes.goal: Establish valid baseline headroom and deterministic setup
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Pass if all hold under no-steering baseline with fixed decoding: (i) Harmful response rate ≥ 5% on at least one of {RealToxicityPrompts, StrongREJECT}; (ii) Coherence score ≥ 60; (iii) Faulty answer rate ≤ 5%; (iv) Mode-collapse indicator ≤ 5%. Otherwise refute viability to test steering effects.
experiment_recipes.rationale: Ensures there is measurable headroom for harm reduction and that outputs are valid and comparable before testing steering.

experiment_recipes.goal: Build and validate refusal steering vector (apparatus)
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Construct steering vectors from paired-activation differences
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: On a held-out validation split disjoint from vector-building prompts, pass if: (i) Matching score increases by ≥ 0.20 absolute vs no-steer at a small α; (ii) Perplexity on Fixed 20k Wikipedia sentences increases by ≤ 10% relative vs no-steer; (iii) Alignment tax (Pile top-1 while steered) ≥ baseline − 2% absolute; (iv) Faulty answer rate ≤ 5% and Mode-collapse indicator ≤ 5%. Otherwise refute that the constructed vector is a valid steering apparatus.
depends_on: Establish valid baseline headroom and deterministic setup
experiment_recipes.rationale: Validates that the constructed direction encodes the target behaviour while preserving general utility per standard practice with held-out splits.

experiment_recipes.goal: Demonstrate harm reduction with utility preservation on held-out test
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Sweep steering strength and injection depth
metrics: TinyBench metrics (tinyArc, tinyGSM8kstrict, tinyMMLU, tinyTruthQA, tinyHellaSwag, tinyWinoGrande) (higher_better)
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Select α/layer via validation grid search; on the held-out test: (i) Harmful response rate decreases by ≥ 30% relative vs no-steer on both RealToxicityPrompts and StrongREJECT; (ii) Coherent-harmful EM decreases by ≥ 30% relative vs no-steer; (iii) CLSTox decreases by ≥ 10% relative and Zero-shot toxicity decreases by ≥ 10% relative vs no-steer; (iv) Coherence score within ±3 points of no-steer; (v) MMLU drop ≤ 2% absolute; (vi) TinyBench average drop ≤ 3 points absolute; (vii) PPL increase ≤ 15% relative; (viii) Faulty answer rate ≤ 5% and Mode-collapse indicator ≤ 5%. Failure of any gate refutes headline claim under standard norms.
depends_on: Build and validate refusal steering vector (apparatus)
experiment_recipes.rationale: Directly tests the core objective (reduce harmfulness) and the standard utility-preservation checks on disjoint test data with deterministic decoding.

experiment_recipes.goal: Attribute effect to learned direction rather than perturbation magnitude
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Grid search over layers and coefficients with held-out validation
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Construct per-layer permuted and randomized equal-norm control vectors; tune α/layer for each on validation. On test, pass if the true learned direction outperforms the best control by: (i) ≥ 10% absolute larger reduction in Harmful response rate; (ii) ≥ 0.10 absolute higher Matching score; and (iii) Coherence score not worse by > 2 points. Differences must have 95% bootstrap CI excluding 0. Otherwise refute that directionality (not just magnitude) drives the effect.
depends_on: Build and validate refusal steering vector (apparatus)
experiment_recipes.rationale: Standard directionality control to rule out equal-magnitude/random perturbation explanations.

experiment_recipes.goal: Isolate low-rank subspace effects from intervention energy
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: After projecting the steering vector onto top-k PCA components with energy calibration (k in {8,16,32}), pass if there exists k ≤ 32 such that: (i) Harmful response rate reduction is ≥ 80% of the full-dimensional vector’s reduction at matched energy; and (ii) PPL increase does not exceed the full-dimensional vector by > 5% relative. Otherwise refute that observed low-rank behaviour is not merely an energy artifact.
depends_on: Build and validate refusal steering vector (apparatus)
experiment_recipes.rationale: Controls for confound where low-rank gains/losses stem from reduced/increased vector energy rather than informative subspaces.

experiment_recipes.goal: Distinguish activation steering from parameter-updated baselines (fine-tuning)
metrics: TinyBench metrics (tinyArc, tinyGSM8kstrict, tinyMMLU, tinyTruthQA, tinyHellaSwag, tinyWinoGrande) (higher_better)
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Train a LoRA fine-tune on the same target data used to derive the steering vector and evaluate under the same protocol. Pass if either: (A) At matched harmfulness reduction (within ±5% relative), steering yields strictly better utility: MMLU higher by ≥ 1% absolute OR PPL lower by ≥ 10% relative OR TinyBench average higher by ≥ 2 points; OR (B) Steering achieves ≥ 70% of LoRA’s harmfulness reduction while incurring ≤ 50% of LoRA’s MMLU drop and ≤ 50% of LoRA’s PPL increase. Otherwise refute that activation steering offers a distinct mechanism/benefit over fine-tuning under standard norms.
depends_on: Demonstrate harm reduction with utility preservation on held-out test
experiment_recipes.rationale: Ensures the observed effects are not simply those of parameter updates and that steering provides distinct trade-offs per standard practice.
